title: Raspberry Peanut Butter Smoothie
subtitle: Daily breakfast
desc: Your go-to weekday breakfast. 2/3 of the original recipe — blended and ready in 2 minutes.
steps: Add all ingredients to a blender.
Blend on high for 30–45 seconds until completely smooth.
Taste — add a little honey if you want more sweetness.
Pour and drink immediately, or seal in a flask for up to 4 hours.
tip: Running low on protein powder? Add an extra teaspoon of peanut butter per 5g of powder you're short to keep the calories roughly the same.

title: Overnight Oats
subtitle: Breakfast
desc: Prep on Sunday night, grab from the fridge all week. Your smoothie ingredients in a jar.
steps: Combine oats, almond milk and yoghurt in a jar or container. Stir well.
Swirl the peanut butter in — don't mix fully, you want a ripple effect.
Seal and refrigerate overnight (or up to 3 days).
In the morning, top with berries and a drizzle of honey. Eat cold.
tip: Batch tip: Make 5 jars on Sunday evening. They keep well in the fridge until Friday.

title: Granola with Yoghurt & Fruit
subtitle: Breakfast
desc: No prep at all — just assemble. Watch the granola brand: calorie counts vary widely.
steps: Spoon Greek yoghurt into a bowl.
Add berries on top.
Sprinkle granola over just before eating — keeps it crunchy.
tip: Granola warning: Check the label before buying. Some granola runs to 480+ kcal per 100g. Aim for under 420 kcal/100g and measure to 60g.

title: Avocado on Toast
subtitle: Breakfast
desc: Two slices, a whole avocado, and five minutes. High in healthy fats and genuinely filling.
steps: Toast the bread to your liking.
Halve and stone the avocado. Scoop flesh into a bowl.
Add lemon juice, salt and pepper. Mash with a fork — keep it chunky.
Spread generously over toast. Finish with chilli flakes.
tip: Ripe avocado test: Gently press the skin near the stem — it should give slightly. A hard avocado needs 1–2 days on the windowsill.

title: Porridge with Peanut Butter
subtitle: Breakfast
desc: Warm, sustaining, and ideal after a morning gym session. The peanut butter makes it genuinely satisfying.
steps: Combine oats and milk in a saucepan over medium heat.
Stir constantly for 4–5 minutes until thick and creamy.
Remove from heat. Stir in peanut butter until melted through.
Pour into a bowl. Top with sliced banana and a drizzle of honey.
tip: Microwave version: Oats + milk in a deep bowl, 2.5 mins on high, stir halfway. Stir in peanut butter afterwards.

title: Chicken & Rice Bowl
subtitle: Lunch — Mon / Wed / Fri
desc: Batch cook on Sunday. Five containers each, ready to grab and reheat in 3 minutes all week.
steps: Season chicken with salt, pepper and garlic powder. Bake at 200°C for 22–25 mins or pan fry. Rest then slice.
Cook rice, drain and cool completely before portioning.
Divide into labelled containers — Jon's are bigger. Add veg on the day to avoid sogginess.
Mix yoghurt and lemon juice in a small pot separately. Add at lunchtime.
tip: Label your containers. Jon's portions are noticeably larger — worth marking them on Sunday.

title: Greek Salad
subtitle: Lunch — Tue / Thu option A
desc: No cooking needed. Prep takes 5 minutes. A proper Greek salad with a warm pitta.
steps: Chop cucumber into chunks, halve the tomatoes, slice onion and pepper thinly.
Arrange all veg in a bowl or container.
Add cubed feta and olives on top.
Drizzle with olive oil and lemon juice. Season with oregano, salt and pepper.
Serve with a warm wholegrain pitta.
tip: No-pitta option: Skip the pitta to save ~140 kcal — brings Jon to ~387 kcal and Jo to ~348 kcal, leaving more room for the evening meal.

title: Salade Niçoise
subtitle: Lunch — Tue / Thu option B
desc: A proper French classic. Tuna and eggs make it genuinely filling — lighter than the Greek salad without the pitta.
steps: Boil eggs for 8 minutes for a just-set yolk. Cool in cold water, peel and halve.
Blanch green beans in boiling water for 3–4 mins. Drain and run under cold water.
Make the dressing: whisk together olive oil, red wine vinegar, Dijon mustard, crushed garlic, salt and pepper.
Arrange leaves on a plate. Add beans, tomatoes, cucumber and onion.
Top with flaked tuna, egg halves and olives. Drizzle with dressing.
dressing: 1 tsp olive oil  •  1 tsp red wine vinegar  •  ½ tsp Dijon mustard  •  1 small garlic clove, crushed  •  salt & pepper
tip: Batch tip: Boil a full batch of eggs on Sunday — they keep unpeeled in the fridge for 5 days. Add a small pitta for ~+140 kcal if needed.

title: Halloumi & Roasted Pepper Salad
subtitle: Lunch — occasional swap
desc: Griddled halloumi on a bed of spinach and roasted peppers. Warm, satisfying and ready in 10 minutes.
steps: Pat halloumi slices dry with kitchen paper.
Heat a non-stick griddle or frying pan over high heat. Spray lightly with olive oil.
Griddle halloumi 1.5–2 mins each side until golden and charred. Do not move it while cooking.
Arrange spinach and roasted peppers on a plate. Add olives.
Lay hot halloumi on top. Squeeze over lemon juice and serve immediately.
tip: Don't fry in oil — halloumi absorbs it instantly and the calories rocket. A dry or lightly sprayed pan gives a better crust anyway.

title: The Lean Fry-Up
subtitle: Weekend treat
desc: All the satisfaction of a fried breakfast, calorie-counted so you know exactly where you stand.
steps: Grill sausages and halved tomato under a medium-high grill for 12–15 mins, turning sausages halfway.
Grill bacon for 3–4 mins each side until cooked through.
Spray a non-stick pan with olive oil. Fry eggs over medium heat to your liking.
Warm baked beans in a small saucepan or microwave.
Plate everything up and serve immediately.
tip: Swap one sausage for mushrooms (~10 kcal per 80g) to drop to ~470 kcal and free up room for a small slice of wholegrain toast (~80 kcal).

title: Macaroni Cheese
subtitle: Dinner
desc: A classic baked macaroni cheese — creamy sauce, plenty of cheddar, golden grilled top. Cook the whole dish, then weigh out a portion to hit your calorie target.
steps: Cook the macaroni in a large saucepan of boiling salted water for 8–10 minutes. Drain well and set aside.
Melt the butter over a medium heat in a saucepan slightly larger than the one used for the macaroni. Add the flour and stir to form a roux, cooking for a few minutes.
Gradually whisk in the milk, a little at a time. Cook for 10–15 minutes to a thickened, smooth sauce.
Meanwhile, preheat the grill to hot.
Remove the sauce from the heat, add 175g of the cheddar and stir until melted through.
Add the macaroni to the sauce and mix well. Transfer to a deep ovenproof dish.
Sprinkle over the remaining cheddar and the Parmesan. Grill until browned and bubbling. Serve straightaway.
tip: Portioning for 500 kcal: The whole dish is roughly 2,900 kcal and weighs about 1,550g cooked — around 190 kcal per 100g. Weigh out ~265g for a 500 kcal portion; the rest keeps 2–3 days in the fridge or freezes well as individual portions. These are standard ingredient averages rather than exact product values, so treat the figure as a good estimate.

title: Easy Hummus
subtitle: Side / dip
desc: A dip, not a meal in itself — worth knowing the calories per gram so you can portion it against whatever it's served with.
steps: Put the drained chickpeas in a saucepan and mash with a potato masher until as smooth as possible.
Add the peanut butter (or tahini), garlic, lemon juice, salt, oil and water.
Season with pepper and beat well with a wooden spoon until combined.
tip: Per gram, not per portion: The whole batch is about 777 kcal and weighs roughly 350g — around 220 kcal per 100g (2.2 kcal/g). A sensible 500 kcal plate: ~135g hummus (~300 kcal) + 1 small wholegrain pitta, ~60g (~165 kcal) + a generous handful of carrot, celery and cucumber sticks, ~150g (~35 kcal — veg sticks are cheap enough to be generous with). These are standard ingredient averages rather than exact product values, so treat the figure as a good estimate.

title: Bread and Butter Pudding
subtitle: Weekend treat
desc: Layered buttered bread, sultanas and cinnamon under a baked custard. Cook the whole dish, then weigh out a portion to hit your calorie target.

ingredients.name: White bread
ingredients.note: 8 thick slices, crusts removed if desired

ingredients.name: Custard
ingredients.note: optional, to serve — not counted below

steps: Grease an ovenproof dish (about 23x28cm/9x11in) with butter.
Butter each slice of bread on one side, then cut into triangles.

Arrange a layer of bread, buttered-side up, in the bottom of the dish, then add a layer of sultanas. Sprinkle with a little cinnamon, then repeat the layers of bread and sultanas, sprinkling with cinnamon, until you have used up all of the bread. Finish with a layer of bread, then set aside.
Gently warm the milk and cream in a saucepan over a low heat to scalding point. Do not let it boil.
Crack the eggs into a bowl, add three-quarters of the sugar and lightly whisk until pale. Add the warm milk and cream mixture and stir well, then strain the custard into a bowl.
Pour the custard over the prepared bread layers, sprinkle with nutmeg and the remaining sugar and leave to stand for 30 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 180C/160C Fan/Gas 4.
Bake for 30–40 minutes, or until the custard has set and the top is golden brown.
Serve hot or warm with extra custard or cream.
tip: Portioning for 500 kcal: The whole dish (excluding any custard served alongside, which isn't quantified in the recipe) is roughly 1,800 kcal and weighs about 820g baked — around 220 kcal per 100g. A standard quarter of the dish is ~205g (~450 kcal), already under 500 without any adjustment. If you want to use the full 500 kcal allowance, that's about 228g. These are standard ingredient averages rather than exact product values, so treat the figure as a good estimate.

title: Carrot and Coriander Soup
subtitle: Lunch — freezer standby
desc: An easy, good-for-you soup. Freezes well, so batch it and always have a healthy, filling lunch ready to go — pairs well with a slice of bread.
steps: Heat the oil in a large frying pan and add the onions and carrots. Cook for 3–4 minutes until starting to soften.
Stir in the ground coriander and season with salt and pepper. Cook for 1 minute.
Add the vegetable stock and bring to the boil. Simmer for 10–15 minutes or until the vegetables are tender.
Whizz with a hand blender or in a blender until smooth. Reheat in a saucepan, stir in the fresh coriander and serve.
tip: Official figure, not an estimate: BBC Good Food publish this one directly — 87 kcal per portion, serves 4 (348 kcal for the whole pot). Each portion works out at a generous ~425g bowl, around 20 kcal per 100g — low enough that a big bowl still leaves plenty of room for bread alongside. Freezes well in individual portions.

title: Pizza Dough
subtitle: Basics — makes ~4 bases
desc: A basic yeasted pizza dough. Dough only — calories below don't include toppings, which will add significantly more.
steps: Mix the flour, salt and yeast in a large bowl. Make a well and gradually add the warm water, mixing to a rough dough.
Turn out onto a floured surface and knead until shiny and springy, about 8–10 minutes.
Place in a lightly oiled bowl, cover, and leave somewhere warm until doubled in size, about 1 hour.
Knock back the dough and divide into 4 portions (or fewer, for larger bases).
Roll or stretch each portion out on a floured surface to your preferred thickness.
Preheat the oven to its highest setting (around 240°C/220°C fan) with a baking tray or pizza stone inside.
Top as you like, then slide onto the hot tray/stone and bake for 8–12 minutes until the crust is golden and blistered.
tip: Dough only: The whole batch is roughly 1,840 kcal and weighs about 840g — around 220 kcal per 100g, split here across 4 bases at ~460 kcal each. Toppings (sauce, cheese, etc.) aren't included — add those separately when you know what's going on top. Shaping and bake steps above are standard additions, not part of the original handwritten note.

title: Airfryer Tandoori Chicken Skewers
subtitle: Dinner
desc: Lean, high-protein tandoori-spiced chicken, air-fried and served with a cooling mint and lime yoghurt dip.
steps: Cut the chicken into chunks and place in a bowl.
Add the paprika, cumin, garam masala, turmeric, ground ginger, yoghurt, tomato puree, garlic puree, oil and lemon juice. Mix well to coat.
Thread onto skewers and cook in the airfryer until cooked through and lightly charred — check your airfryer's guide for time and temperature, as this varies by model and chunk size.
Meanwhile, mix the dip ingredients together.
Serve the skewers hot with the mint and lime yoghurt dip.
dressing: 1–2 tbsp fat-free yoghurt  •  juice of 2 limes  •  freshly chopped mint  •  salt and pepper
tip: Estimate, assumptions flagged: Assuming this serves 2 (200g chicken each), the skewers are roughly 300 kcal per serving and the dip is close to negligible (~15 kcal total) — around 315 kcal per person for skewers plus dip. Serving count wasn't specified in the original note, so adjust if it's meant to serve differently. Airfryer time/temperature also isn't given — check your model's guide, as this varies a lot by make and chunk size.

title: Chicken Satay with Peanut Sauce
subtitle: Dinner
desc: Marinated chicken skewers with a rich, generous peanut sauce. The sauce is the calorie-heavy part here — worth serving a modest amount.
steps: Cut the chicken into pieces.
Mix the coconut milk, curry powder, sugar, garlic, ginger, soy sauce, fish sauce and oil in a bowl.
Add the chicken and marinate for at least 20 minutes, preferably overnight.
Combine all the peanut sauce ingredients in a saucepan over medium heat.
Stir until smooth and warm.
Adjust thickness by adding water or coconut milk as needed.
Thread the marinated chicken onto skewers and cook — in the airfryer, or grill/griddle until cooked through and charred.
Serve together once cooked.
tip: Estimate, assumptions flagged: The whole batch (chicken plus the full quantity of peanut sauce) is roughly 2,740 kcal. No serving count was given — assuming this serves 4, that's about 685 kcal per person, which is high mostly because of the rich peanut sauce (over 1,200 kcal on its own). Using half the sauce quantity would bring this down significantly if you want a lighter version. Original method didn't specify a cook method for the chicken beyond skewering — airfryer, grill or griddle all work.

title: Creamy Garlic Chicken
subtitle: Dinner
desc: Air-fried chicken finished in a rich garlic and sun-dried tomato cream sauce. One of the richest dinners in the book — mostly down to the cream.
steps: Sprinkle the chicken with cayenne and cook in the airfryer.
Melt the butter over a medium heat.
Stir in the onion and garlic.
Once translucent, add the sun-dried tomatoes, tomato paste and the remaining spices.
Stir in the heavy cream and spinach and let it simmer for about 5–7 minutes, covered, or until the spinach is wilted.
Stir in the parmesan cheese and add the air-fried chicken to the pan.
tip: Estimate, assumptions flagged: The whole dish is roughly 2,840 kcal. Assuming it serves 4 (matching the 3–4 chicken breasts), that's about 710 kcal per portion — the highest of the dinner-category recipes so far, almost entirely down to the 2 cups of heavy cream (over 1,600 kcal alone). Worth treating as an occasional richer dinner rather than a regular weeknight one, or halving the cream/adding stock to lighten it.

title: Chicken and Leek Pie
subtitle: Dinner
desc: A proper from-scratch pie — creamy chicken and leek filling in homemade shortcrust pastry. Rich and filling; a good candidate for a smaller wedge with extra veg.
steps: Melt the butter in a casserole dish over a low heat.
Add the leek, chicken, herbs and seasoning and cook for 10–12 minutes until the chicken is cooked, the leeks have softened and the mixture is simmering.
Stir in the flour and cook for 3 minutes until the mix resembles a sandy paste.
Pour in the wine and bubble for 1 minute, then stir in the stock, crème fraîche and the mustard.
Cook for 10 minutes until the chicken is cooked through.
Season to taste, remove from the heat and leave to cool completely.
Tip into a container and chill for 2 hours or overnight.
To make the pastry, rub the cold butter into the flour with a large pinch of salt until completely combined.
Add half the beaten egg and 4 tbsp ice-cold water, and bring together into a dough using your hands, adding a little more water if needed.
Knead for a minute so it completely comes together, then chill for 1 hour.
Butter a 20cm loose-bottomed cake tin.
Roll two-thirds of the pastry out until large enough to line the tin with some overhanging.
Use it to line the tin, then spoon in the filling.
Roll out the remaining pastry until large enough to cover the pie.
Brush the edge of the pastry with a little of the remaining beaten egg, then drape over the pie to close it.
Trim the edge, then press with a fork to seal.
Chill until you're ready to cook.
Heat the oven to 200°C with a baking sheet inside.
Brush the pie with some of the remaining beaten egg, then lightly score a criss-cross pattern on top using a sharp knife.
Bake on the hot sheet for 20 minutes, then brush with the rest of the egg, season with sea salt flakes and bake for 15–20 minutes more until deep golden.
Remove from the oven and rest for 10 minutes, then carefully remove from the tin, put on a board and cut into wedges to serve.
tip: Estimate, assumptions flagged: The whole pie is roughly 4,400 kcal, split mostly evenly between the creamy filling and the all-butter pastry. A 20cm pie like this typically serves 6 — that puts each wedge at about 735 kcal, one of the richer dinners in the book. A smaller wedge alongside a big pile of vegetables would bring this down considerably.

title: Jambalaya
subtitle: Dinner
desc: A one-pot Cajun-spiced chicken, chorizo and rice dish. Sits comfortably in the everyday dinner calorie range without any adjustment needed.
steps: Cook the chicken in the airfryer.
Heat the olive oil and fry the diced onion for 3–4 minutes until soft.
Add the thinly sliced red pepper, garlic, chorizo and cajun seasoning and cook for 5 minutes more.
Stir the chicken back in with the rice, tomatoes and chicken stock.
Cover and simmer for 20–25 minutes until the rice is tender.
tip: Estimate: The whole pot is roughly 2,020 kcal. Assuming it serves 4, that's about 505 kcal per portion — a solid everyday dinner figure, no adjustment needed.

title: Mushroom Sauce for Steak
subtitle: Basics — sauce
desc: A rich creamy mushroom sauce to serve over steak. A condiment, not a meal — shown per 100g since serving size varies a lot by how much you pour on.
steps: Melt the butter over a medium heat.
Stir in the mushrooms and garlic. Sauté for 3–4 minutes until the mushrooms are browned.
Stir in the broth, cream, Dijon, Worcestershire, salt and pepper. Continue to stir periodically for 5–8 minutes until the liquid is reduced, thickened and creamy.
Taste, add salt and pepper if needed. Serve over steak and top with additional cracked black pepper if desired — enjoy!
tip: Per gram, not per portion: The whole batch is about 1,190 kcal and weighs roughly 645g — around 185 kcal per 100g. A generous 3 tbsp (~45g) ladled over a steak is about 85 kcal; go easy if you're watching the total.

title: Easy Onion Gravy
subtitle: Basics — sauce
desc: Slow-caramelised onion gravy with red wine and beef stock. A condiment, not a meal — shown per 100g since it's served in variable amounts.
steps: Melt the butter with the olive oil in a large frying pan over a medium heat.
Add the bay leaf and thyme and cook for a minute to infuse the flavours of the herbs.
Add the onions and coat well in the butter and oil.
Sprinkle over the sugar and a big pinch of salt and slowly cook the onions down for 45–50 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sticky and caramelised.
Add the flour and stir well, coating all of the onions.
Cook for a minute then add the wine and vinegar, turn up the heat and reduce by half, about 2 minutes, whisking a little to ensure the flour doesn't lump.
Pour in the stock, bring to the boil and cook for 6–8 minutes, until the gravy is thick enough to coat the back of a spoon.
If it gets too thick, add a splash of water.
Season well and serve.
tip: Per gram, not per portion: The whole batch (before reduction losses from the long cook) is about 810 kcal across roughly 1,360g of ingredients — around 60 kcal per 100g, and simmering down further will concentrate this only slightly since most of the loss is water. A typical ladle (~50g) is around 30 kcal, so it's an easy add-on without much calorie cost.

title: Homemade Burgers
subtitle: Dinner
desc: Simple beef burgers from scratch. Figure below is patty and bun only — toppings, cheese and sauce aren't included.
steps: Tip the beef mince into a bowl with the onion and egg, then mix.
Divide the mixture into 4. Lightly wet your hands. Carefully roll the mixture into balls, each about the same size.
Set in the palm of your hand and gently squeeze down to flatten into patties about 3cm thick. Make sure all the burgers are the same thickness so they cook evenly.
Put on a plate, cover with cling film and leave in the fridge to firm up for at least 30 minutes.
Cook in a hot pan with the oil, or on a griddle/barbecue, until done to your liking.
Serve in the buns.
tip: Estimate, patty + bun only: The 4 burgers (mince, onion, egg, buns) come to roughly 2,400 kcal in total — about 600 kcal each before any cheese, sauce, salad or chips. Add those separately depending on how you serve it.

title: Chicken and Bacon Pasta
subtitle: Dinner
desc: A very rich, creamy tagliatelle with chicken and bacon. By far the highest-calorie dinner in the book — best treated as an occasional dish.

ingredients.name: Stock cube
ingredients.note: mentioned in method but not listed in original ingredients — amount assumed, low calorie impact either way

steps: Heat the oil and butter in a medium saucepan over a low heat and fry the onion for 10 minutes, or until softened and translucent.
Add the garlic and cook for 2 minutes more.
Add the cream, mascarpone, cheese and stock cube.
Give it a stir and add the cooked chicken and bacon to heat through.
Meanwhile, cook the pasta.
Reserve 100ml of the pasta water.
Toss the pasta in the creamy sauce and enough of the reserved water to loosen.
Season with black pepper.
tip: Estimate, assumptions flagged: The whole dish is roughly 4,520 kcal. Assuming it serves 4, that's about 1,130 kcal per portion — by a wide margin the richest dinner in the book, driven by double cream, mascarpone, cheese and bacon together. Worth treating as an occasional meal rather than a regular one, or scaling back the cream/mascarpone if you want to make it a regular. The original note also mentions a stock cube in the method that isn't in the ingredients list — included here as an assumption since it has little calorie impact either way.

title: Ultra Simple Curry
subtitle: Dinner
desc: A flexible spiced tomato, chickpea and paneer curry. Several quantities weren't specified in the original note — treat the figure below as a loose estimate.

ingredients.name: Ginger
ingredients.note: amount not specified — assumed ~1 tbsp grated

steps: Roast the coriander seeds, cumin seeds and cinnamon stick until they smell fragrant.
Grind, then add the turmeric.
Fry the onion.
Add the garlic, ginger and chillies and continue to fry.
Add the spice mix.
Add the tinned tomatoes, chickpeas and paneer. Cook.
Add a squeeze of lime and coriander leaves to finish (optional).
tip: Estimate, several quantities assumed: Garlic, ginger, paneer and lime amounts weren't specified in the original note — assumed reasonable quantities to reach the roughly 1,260 kcal total, which works out at about 315 kcal per portion assuming it serves 4. This is one of the lower-calorie dinners in the book, but the estimate is looser than most since so much was left to taste — treat it as a starting point rather than a precise figure.

title: Dhal
subtitle: Dinner
desc: A warming spiced red lentil dhal with coconut milk. Freezes well and reheats easily.
steps: Melt the butter. Add the mustard seeds and cover. When the seeds pop, add the onion, garlic and ginger.
Cook uncovered for 7–8 minutes.
Stir in the turmeric and green chillies and cook for 1–2 minutes.
Add the lentils and cook, stirring frequently, for 2 minutes, until the lentils begin to turn translucent.
Stir in the water, coconut milk and salt. Bring to the boil then reduce the heat and simmer for 40 minutes.
tip: Estimate: The whole pot is roughly 1,945 kcal and weighs about 1,675g — around 116 kcal per 100g. Assuming it serves 4, that's about 485 kcal per portion, a solid everyday dinner figure. Freezes well in individual portions.

title: Prawn and Pea Risotto
subtitle: Dinner
desc: A classic creamy risotto with prawn-shell stock, peas and lemon. A bit of a labour of love, but worth it.
steps: Peel the prawns, keeping the heads and shells. Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a large saucepan and fry the prawn shells and heads with the sliced chilli until toasted and changed colour. Pour in the stock, bring to the boil, then turn down to a simmer.
Melt half the butter over a medium heat.
Stir in the onion and sweat gently for 8–10 minutes until soft but not coloured, stirring occasionally.
Stir the rice into the onions until completely coated in the butter, then stir continuously until the rice is shiny and the edges of the grain start to look transparent.
Pour in the wine and simmer until totally evaporated.
Add the stock, a ladleful at a time, stirring with each addition until absorbed.
Stir through the prawns and peas.

Continue adding stock a ladleful at a time and stirring the rice over a low heat for 25–30 minutes until the rice is cooked al dente. The risotto should be creamy and slightly soupy — when you draw a wooden spoon through it, there should be a wake that holds for a few moments but not longer.
Cook until the prawns change colour.
Stir through the chopped chilli, lemon juice and remaining olive oil.
Let the risotto rest for a few minutes, then serve, topped with the lemon zest.
tip: Estimate: The whole dish is roughly 2,560 kcal. Assuming it serves 4, that's about 640 kcal per portion — a fairly rich dinner between the olive oil, butter and rice, but not an outlier for a risotto.

title: Pulled Pork Tacos
subtitle: Dinner
desc: Slow-cooked citrus and spice pulled pork with quick-pickled red onions. Explicitly serves 8 in the original note.

ingredients.name: White wine vinegar or cider vinegar
Corn tacos, warmed
ingredients.note: to serve — not quantified, not counted below

ingredients.name: Little gem lettuce
ingredients.note: to serve — not quantified, not counted below

ingredients.name: Soured cream
ingredients.note: to serve — not quantified, not counted below

steps: Put the marinade ingredients in a large, zip-sealed freezer bag and squish until well combined. Add the pork and onion, ensuring they're well coated. Seal and put in the fridge overnight.

Heat the oven to 140°C. Transfer the pork and its marinade to a medium casserole dish. Cover with a lid and place in the oven for 4–5 hours or until the pork is very tender and falls apart when poked with a fork.

To make the pickled onions, put the sliced red onions in a heatproof bowl with just-boiled water and leave to stand for 10 minutes. Drain well, then stir in the white wine vinegar and caster sugar. Stand for at least 10 minutes before serving.

Drain the pork in a colander, reserving the marinade, then transfer the pork to a board. Shred the pork with two forks, drizzle over 4–5 tbsp of the reserved marinade, and serve from the board with the pickled red onions, warmed corn tacos, shredded lettuce and soured cream.
tip: Serves 8, as stated in the original note: The pork and pickled onion together are roughly 4,200 kcal, working out at about 525 kcal per portion before you add tacos, lettuce or soured cream — none of which were given a quantity, so add those separately based on how you serve it.

title: Crispy Chinese Fakeaway
subtitle: Dinner
desc: Cornflour-coated crispy chicken with a sweet-savoury sauce, stir-fried veg and rice.
steps: Cut the chicken breast into bite-sized pieces and cover in salt, pepper, cornflour and garlic powder.
Wash the rice until the water runs clear, then add enough water to come up to your first knuckle from the rice and bring to a simmer.
Add all of the sauce ingredients to a jar or bowl and combine.
Heat the oil to a high heat and add the chicken pieces in batches for a few minutes each side until golden and crispy.
Dice the vegetables and add to the pan for a few minutes, then add the sauce and cornflour slurry (remove the rice and steam).
Add the chicken back and coat everything.
Add rice to a small ramekin or bowl and add to your plate, plate up the rest of the food and top with the green parts of the spring onions and sesame seeds.
tip: Estimate, assumptions flagged: The whole batch (excluding rice, which is listed per-portion) is roughly 1,190 kcal. With 3 chicken breasts, assuming it serves 3, that's about 397 kcal per portion, plus 175 kcal for the 50g rice per portion — around 570 kcal total per plate. Sesame oil and rice vinegar quantities weren't specified in the original note, so 1 tbsp of each is assumed; frying oil quantity is also assumed.

title: Roasted Aubergine Salad
subtitle: Lunch
desc: Roasted aubergine, red onion, celery and cherry tomatoes over orzo, finished with feta and pine nuts.
steps: Cook the orzo according to packet instructions.
Heat the oven to 200°C.
Top and tail the aubergine and cut it in half widthways, then into eighths lengthwise.
Lay the aubergine pieces on their side in a medium baking tin and prebake for 10 minutes, then turn to the other side and carry on baking for another 10 minutes.

Add the red onion wedges, celery and pine nuts to the tray. Stir in the olive oil and minced garlic. Season with the dried herbs, smoked paprika, chilli and a generous amount of salt and pepper. Return to the oven and bake for another 20 minutes, giving the vegetables a good stir and adding the balsamic vinegar halfway through.
Plate the roast vegetables on top of the orzo. Sprinkle with fresh herbs and dot with feta cheese.
tip: Estimate, assumptions flagged: The whole dish is roughly 1,500 kcal. Feta quantity wasn't specified, so ~50g is assumed. Assuming it serves 3 (240g dry orzo is a substantial batch), that's about 500 kcal per portion, a good fit alongside the other lunch salads.

title: Traditional Lasagne
subtitle: Dinner
desc: A classic beef or lamb lasagne with a cheese sauce. Serves 4–6 as stated in the original note.

ingredients.name: Cheese sauce
ingredients.note: recipe not specified — assumed standard bechamel-style

steps: Heat the oil in a large pan and gently fry the onion until softened, stir in the meat and cook until brown. Add the tomatoes, stock, tomato puree, garlic and herbs and bring to the boil. Simmer for 20–25 minutes. Season to taste.
Arrange layers of meat sauce, cheese sauce and lasagne sheets, finishing with cheese sauce. Scatter the surface with the grated cheese.
Bake at 180°C, 350°F, gas mark 4 for 50–60 minutes.
tip: Estimate, one assumption flagged: The cheese sauce recipe wasn't included, so a standard homemade cheese sauce (~165 kcal/100ml) is assumed. On that basis the whole lasagne is roughly 2,800 kcal — assuming 5 portions (the middle of the stated serves 4–6), that's about 560 kcal per portion.

title: Vegetable Lasagne
subtitle: Dinner
desc: A veg-packed lasagne with aubergine, courgette and peppers under a from-scratch cheese sauce. Generous on the olive oil — one of the richer vegetarian dinners.
steps: Slice the aubergines and half the courgettes, place in a colander or sieve, sprinkle with 2 tsp salt, and leave to stand for 30 minutes. Rinse in cold water, pat dry with kitchen paper.
Peel and chop the onion, then peel and crush the garlic. Drain the canned tomatoes.
Heat 4 tbsp of the oil in a large pan, fry the onion and garlic for 10 minutes until soft and golden.

De-seed and slice the peppers. Slice the small tomatoes, reserving the middle slices for topping. Add the tomato ends, drained tomatoes, tomato puree, aubergines, prepared courgettes, peppers, salt and pepper, and bring to the boil. Cover and simmer for 15 minutes.

To make the sauce, grate the cheese, mix the milk and flour in a pan, and bring to the boil, stirring continuously. Add the cheese and mustard, stirring until the cheese melts. Season and remove from the heat.
Spoon half the tomato sauce into a large (2L) ovenproof dish, cover with half the lasagne sheets in a single layer and half the cheese sauce. Repeat the layers once more.
With a sharp knife, pare thin strips of skin from the remaining courgettes. Slice the courgettes thinly for topping.
Arrange the reserved tomato slices and courgette strips on top. Brush with the remaining 2 tbsp olive oil.
Bake at 375°F, 190°C, gas mark 5, for 30–40 minutes until the lasagne is soft and the cheese is bubbling.
Serve with a crisp green salad.
tip: Estimate, serving count assumed: No serving count was given, so 4–6 (matching its Traditional Lasagne counterpart) is assumed. The whole dish is roughly 2,850 kcal — assuming 5 portions, that's about 570 kcal per portion. The 90ml (6 tbsp) of olive oil is a significant chunk of that; using less for frying and brushing would bring the total down.

title: Chicken Korma
subtitle: Dinner
desc: A rich, mild, from-scratch korma with creamed coconut and ground almonds. Serves 4–6 as stated — one of the richer curries, mostly from the oil and coconut.
steps: Cut each chicken piece in half, separating leg from thigh and each breast in two (or use boneless breast joints cut in half).
Mix with the ginger and yoghurt and leave to marinate in a cool place for 2–4 hours or in the fridge overnight.
Place the chopped onion, red chillies and garlic in a liquidiser or food processor and liquidise to a smooth paste, adding a little water if needed (or chop as finely as possible by hand).

Heat the 5 tbsp oil over a medium heat and fry the sliced onions until golden brown. Remove the pan from the heat and, using a slotted spoon, transfer the onions to another dish, leaving any remaining oil in the pan.
Place the pan the onions were fried in over a medium heat and add the other 2 tbsp oil.

When hot, add the ground coriander, powdered pepper, garam masala and turmeric, stir rapidly (take the pan off the heat if the oil is too hot), and add the chicken and marinade. Adjust the heat to medium-high and fry the chicken for about 10 minutes, stirring frequently.
Add the liquidised spice paste and continue to fry for 6–8 minutes on a low heat.
Add the water and the coconut and bring to the boil. Stir until the coconut dissolves. Add the fried onion slices and salt.
Reduce the heat to low, cover the pan and simmer until the chicken is tender, 25–30 minutes. Sprinkle the ground almonds on and mix well. Remove from the heat and add the lemon juice.
Serve with pilau rice (bought or home-spiced).
tip: Estimate: The whole dish is roughly 3,570 kcal. Assuming it serves 5 (the middle of the stated serves 4–6), that's about 715 kcal per portion — one of the richer dinners in the book, mostly from the 7 tbsp of cooking oil plus the creamed coconut and ground almonds. Figure doesn't include the pilau rice served alongside.

title: Chilli con Carne Vegetariana
subtitle: Dinner
desc: A vegetarian chilli with kidney beans and green lentils. Serves 4 as stated — a moderate-calorie, everyday dinner.

ingredients.name: Red kidney beans
ingredients.note: soaked, cooked and drained, or 2×425g cans

steps: Heat the oil in a large saucepan and fry the onion for 10 minutes, then add the garlic and tomatoes.
Drain the red kidney beans and lentils, reserving the liquid. Add the beans and lentils to the tomato mixture, together with the paprika and chilli powder.
Simmer for about 15 minutes, then season with salt, pepper and sugar, and serve, garnished with coriander.
tip: Estimate: The whole pot is roughly 1,410 kcal. Serving as stated (4), that's about 355 kcal per portion — a moderate, everyday-friendly vegetarian dinner.

title: Prawn Cocktail
subtitle: Side / starter
desc: A retro classic — prawns in a Marie Rose-style sauce over shredded lettuce. Light enough to work as a starter or a light lunch side.
steps: Blend the sauce ingredients (mayonnaise, ketchup, cream, tabasco, Worcestershire sauce and lemon juice) together and fold in the prawns.
Wash and finely shred the lettuce and place in four glass dishes.
Pile the cocktail mixture on top and garnish with slices of cucumber slotted onto the rim of the glass.
tip: Estimate: The whole recipe is roughly 555 kcal. Assuming it serves 4 (the classic four-glass-dish version), that's about 140 kcal per portion — a light starter rather than a main.

title: Coronation Chicken Sauce
subtitle: Basics — sauce
desc: A quick curried mayonnaise sauce to stir through cooked chicken. Chicken quantity wasn't specified in the original note, so shown per 100g of sauce.

ingredients.name: Cooked chicken
ingredients.note: cut into small chunks — amount not specified, add to taste

steps: Stir the mayonnaise, cream, sieved apricot jam and curry powder together.
Add the cooked chicken, cut into small chunks, and stir through to coat.
tip: Per gram, not per portion: The sauce alone (before chicken) is about 475 kcal and weighs roughly 104g — around 455 kcal per 100g. Since the chicken quantity wasn't given, total calories depend entirely on how much chicken you stir through; 2 tbsp of sauce coating ~150g of chicken would add roughly 250 kcal for the chicken on top of about 115 kcal of sauce.

title: White Coffee
subtitle: Daily drink
desc: Coffee with a splash of frothed semi-skimmed milk. A handy everyday figure to log without thinking twice.
steps: Make the coffee as usual.
Add a splash of semi-skimmed milk and froth if you like.
tip: Everyday figure: ~80 kcal for a normal splash of frothed semi-skimmed milk. A bigger milk pour will push this up — worth a rough gauge if you're having more than one a day.

title: Sugar-Free Sweets
subtitle: Snack
desc: A low-calorie way to satisfy a sweet craving — worth logging by the sweet rather than guessing.
steps: Eat as many as you've counted, and log by the sweet.
tip: Handy for tracking: ~9 kcal per sweet — cheap enough calorie-wise that a few won't dent a day's total, but worth logging honestly if you're having a handful.

title: Felafel in Pitta Pockets
subtitle: Lunch
desc: Homemade felafel, shallow-fried and stuffed into wholewheat pittas with tomato and cucumber. Serves 4 as stated in the original note.

ingredients.name: Chickpeas
ingredients.note: soaked, cooked and drained, or 425g canned, drained

steps: Mash the chickpeas thoroughly, then add the egg, onion, parsley, garlic and spices. Mix well; season to taste with salt and pepper.
Shape the mixture into balls about the size of chestnuts, then coat in flour.
Put the pitta bread to warm under the grill or in a moderate oven.
Pour enough oil into a frying pan to cover the base thinly, and when it is hot fry the felafel for 3 minutes on each side, until golden brown. Drain well on kitchen paper.
Cut each pitta bread in half across the centre, then fill each with felafel, sliced tomato and cucumber, and garnish with lemon and fennel.
tip: Estimate: The whole recipe is roughly 1,545 kcal. Serving as stated (4), that's about 385 kcal per portion, a solid fit alongside the other lunches. Note from the original recipe: if using canned chickpeas (softer than home-cooked), you may need a few fresh breadcrumbs to firm the mixture up enough to shape.

title: Cheese Scones
subtitle: Baking
desc: Quick savoury scones, best served warm. Makes about 8, so worth doubling if baking for more than a couple of people.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F (218°C, gas 7).
Sift the flour and salt into a mixing bowl.
Cut the fat into small pieces and add to the flour.
Rub in the fat with fingertips until no lumps are left — it should look like breadcrumbs.
Stir in the cheese, then add the milk, 1 tbsp at a time, stirring well with a knife until it begins to stick together.
Using one hand, collect the mixture together and knead lightly to form a soft dough.
Turn onto a lightly floured board, form into a flat round shape, and roll until 3cm thick.
Cut into 5cm rounds.
Place on a greased baking tin, brush with milk.
Bake towards the top of the oven for about 10 minutes until golden brown.
Allow to cool on a rack.
tip: Estimate: The whole batch is roughly 1,210 kcal. Makes about 8 scones per the original note — that's about 150 kcal each. Extra cheese can be sprinkled on before baking (not counted above). For fruit scones, the original note says to omit the cheese and add 40g sugar and 50g currants instead — a sweeter variant not costed separately here.

title: Banana Bread
subtitle: Baking
desc: A simple one-bowl banana loaf. Assumed to cut into 10 slices.
steps: Turn the oven on to 175°C.
Grease a loaf tin.
Put all ingredients except the bananas in a bowl and mix.
Add the bananas and mix again.
Put in the loaf tin.
Pop on the middle shelf of the oven.
Bake for 45 minutes.
tip: Estimate: The whole loaf is roughly 2,425 kcal. Cut into 10 slices (a typical loaf), that's about 240 kcal per slice.

title: Apple Pie
subtitle: Baking
desc: A classic double-crust apple pie using a full batch of shortcrust pastry. Assumed to serve 6.

ingredients.name: Shortcrust pastry
ingredients.note: one full batch — see the Pastry recipe (Basics)

steps: Preheat the oven to 425°F (218°C).
Peel, core and slice the cooking apples.
Line a plate with the pastry, as for a jam tart.
Fill the pastry with the apple slices and sugar.
Brush the edges with beaten egg or milk.
Lift on a lid of pastry.
Seal the edges by pressing with a spoon handle, then frill by pressing with one finger and lifting the next bit with a finger on the other hand, all the way round.
Brush with egg or milk and sprinkle with sugar.
Cook for 20–30 minutes.
tip: Estimate, pastry quantity uncertain: "A full batch of pastry" is assumed to mean the standard Pastry recipe (100g fat, 200g flour) — on that basis the whole pie is roughly 2,180 kcal, and assuming it serves 6, about 365 kcal per slice. The handwritten side notes on the original page suggest a bigger batch (8oz/227g margarine, 16oz/454g flour, no lard) for a larger pie dish, which would roughly double the pastry calories — worth bearing in mind if that's the version actually used.

title: Pancakes
subtitle: Baking
desc: Classic thin pancakes fried in lard. Figure below is batter only — sugar, lemon or golden syrup to serve aren't counted.

ingredients.name: Sugar, lemon, golden syrup
ingredients.note: to serve — not quantified, not counted below

steps: Sift the flour and salt into a bowl.
Make a hole in the centre of the flour and break in the egg.
Add 2 tablespoons of the liquid and, working from the centre, stir until all the ingredients are well mixed.
Add half the remaining liquid, a little at a time, and beat gently until the batter is smooth.
Stir in the remaining liquid.
Put a small piece of lard in the frying pan and heat until it begins to "haze".
Pour in a little batter, using a jug or ladle. Tip the pan to cover the base.
Fry over a moderate heat until the underneath is golden.
Loosen the edges and turn over.
Cook until the second side is golden.
tip: Estimate, batter only: The batter plus frying fat is roughly 705 kcal. Assuming this makes 6 pancakes, that's about 120 kcal each before sugar, lemon or golden syrup — add those separately depending on how you serve it. The original note says oil can be used instead of lard, which would lower this slightly.

title: Kuth's Scotch Pancakes
subtitle: Baking
desc: Thick, bubbly drop scones fried in butter. A handwritten family recipe.
steps: Mix the flour, sugar, baking powder, egg and milk into a thick batter.
Fry in a little knob of butter over a medium heat; when spread round the pan, wipe with kitchen roll.
Cook until the batter bubbles and the edges look set — it should be quite thick.
Squidge when turned to check it's cooked through, then flip and cook the other side.
tip: Estimate: The whole batch is roughly 1,240 kcal. Assuming it makes 12 small pancakes, that's about 105 kcal each.

title: Banana and Oat Pancakes
subtitle: Breakfast
desc: Blender pancakes made from banana and oats, no flour needed. Assumed to serve 2 as a breakfast stack.
steps: Add all of the ingredients to a blender and blend on high until completely smooth, about 30 seconds to 1 minute.
Let the batter sit in your blender while you heat your pan up.
Cook.
tip: Estimate: The whole batch is roughly 1,000 kcal. Assuming it serves 2 (a stack of about 4 pancakes each), that's about 500 kcal per serving — a good fit alongside the other breakfasts.

title: Pastry
subtitle: Basics — shortcrust
desc: The standard shortcrust used for pies, tarts and sausage rolls in this book. The ratio is always half fat to flour.

ingredients.name: Cold water
ingredients.note: a little at a time, ideally with an ice cube added

steps: Cut the fat into small pieces and rub in.
Add cold water, a little at a time, stirring with a knife until it begins to stick together.
Draw together with your hand, and knead gently.
Place on a floured board and roll out to about 1/2cm thick.
Handle as little as possible — the pastry should be kept cool. An ice cube added to the water helps.
tip: Per gram, not per portion: One batch (100g fat, 200g flour) is about 1,540 kcal and weighs roughly 350g — around 440 kcal per 100g. This is the pastry referenced as "a full batch" or "half batch" in the Apple Pie and Jam Tart recipes.

title: Jam Tart
subtitle: Baking
desc: A large jam tart using half a batch of pastry. Assumed cut into 6 slices. Can be swapped for golden syrup (syrup tart) or made as small individual tarts.

ingredients.name: Shortcrust pastry
ingredients.note: half a batch — see the Pastry recipe (Basics)

steps: Heat the oven to 425°F (218°C).
Grease a large oven-proof plate.
Use half a batch of pastry.
Place the dough on a floured board, flatten and shape into a round.
Roll out into a round slightly larger than the plate, lift over the rolling pin onto the plate, supporting it well.
Ease the pastry to follow the shape of the plate, without stretching it.
Holding the plate up, cut off excess pastry.
Spread 3–4 rounded tablespoonfuls of jam.
Place the tart on a baking sheet and bake near the top of the oven for 15–20 minutes.
For a syrup tart: sprinkle some oats on the pastry base before adding warmed golden syrup instead of jam.
For small jam tarts: use a pastry cutter with a full batch of pastry, 1 small teaspoon of jam in each tart, and cook for 12 minutes.
tip: Estimate: The tart (half-batch pastry plus jam) is roughly 970 kcal. Cut into 6 slices, that's about 160 kcal each. The syrup tart variant would be similar or slightly higher since golden syrup is a touch more calorie-dense than jam; small tarts work out to roughly the same per-teaspoon-of-jam basis.

title: Fruit Salad
subtitle: Dessert
desc: Fresh fruit in a light orange syrup. No fruit quantities were given beyond "a selection as available" — treat the figure below as a loose guide only.

ingredients.name: Orange
ingredients.note: peel used for syrup, flesh added to salad

ingredients.name: Selection of fruits
ingredients.note: e.g. apple, pear, grapes, kiwi, banana — quantity not specified, assumed ~600g mixed

steps: Peel the orange, place the skin, sugar and water in a saucepan and bring to the boil (the sugar will dissolve).
Leave to cool.
Prepare the fruits as necessary — peel kiwi, wash and deseed grapes and apples.
Slice the fruits.
Place the fruit in the syrup in a glass dish.
tip: Loose estimate — quantities largely unspecified: The original note leaves the fruit selection and amounts to what's available, so ~600g of mixed fruit is assumed to reach the roughly 860 kcal total, working out at about 170 kcal per portion assuming it serves 5. Treat this as a rough guide rather than a precise figure. Note from the original recipe: leave bananas until serving as they're better fresh, and tinned fruit (using its syrup instead of making your own) works if fresh is short.

title: Carrot Cake
subtitle: Baking
desc: A spiced carrot cake with walnuts and cream cheese frosting. Assumed cut into 14 slices. Raisins are listed but the original note says "I don't use these" — excluded below.
steps: Cream the butter/margarine and sugar together, using a mixer or a wooden spoon and plenty of elbow grease.
Add the eggs a little at a time, beating well after each addition.
Sieve the flour, bicarbonate of soda, baking powder, cinnamon and salt together.
Fold the dry ingredients into the egg mixture.
Add the carrots, walnuts and raisins if used.
Mix well and spoon into a well-greased tin (the mixture is too stiff to pour).
Bake at 180°C (350°F), gas mark 4, for 45–50 minutes.
Cool in the tin for 10 minutes before turning out.

For the frosting: allow the cream cheese and butter to stand at room temperature. Beat with the lemon rind until creamy. Gradually add the icing sugar, beating well. Spread on the cooled cake and allow to become firm before cutting.
tip: Estimate, raisins excluded per the original note: The cake plus frosting is roughly 5,580 kcal. Cut into 14 slices, that's about 400 kcal per slice — one of the richer bakes in the book, mostly from the icing sugar and butter in the frosting.

title: Scott's Flapjacks
subtitle: Baking
desc: Simple oat flapjacks baked in a 30x20cm tin. Assumed cut into 14 pieces.

ingredients.name: Demerara sugar
ingredients.note: or any brown sugar to hand

steps: Grease a tin, 30x20cm (or a foil-lined tin adjusted to size, held down with some rice or pasta if needed).
Melt the margarine, sugar and syrup in a pan.
Stir in the oats.
Spread evenly in the tin.
Bake for 20 minutes or until golden brown, at 180°C, 350°F, gas mark 4.
tip: Estimate: The whole tin is roughly 2,290 kcal. Cut into 14 pieces, that's about 165 kcal each.
